title: Gujarat has a stepwell built like an inverted temple
body: Rani-ki-Vav in Patan, Gujarat, was built as a memorial in the 11th century CE. Seven levels of stairs descend towards the well, past more than 500 major sculptures carved into the stone.
takeaway: The stairs let people reach water at different depths as the water level changed.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Committee, Decision 38 COM 8B.25 (2014)
visual: a view down the carved stone terraces of Rani-ki-Vav, with descending stairways framed by sculpted pillars
